brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.requirement: Wall clock form: a body that mounts on a wall
requirements.evidence: Two Hex base · Full pieces at cells (0,0,0) and (2,0,0) form the body. No wall-mount accessory was added (keyhole hanger or French cleat exist in the catalog but are not in the build), so it is not yet mounted to a wall.

One rotating axle (axle:0#0,0#0) spans the empty cell (1,0,0) between rod sockets on each base (hex-acc-rod on (0,0,0) slot 0 and (2,0,0) slot 3). A filament spool hangs on it as a turning element. The configurator has no clock-hand part, so the spool stands in for a hand; it is not a shaped hour or minute hand and only one hand exists. Rotation itself is not verified by the configurator.

requirements.requirement: Hands tell the time (hour and minute hands, dial with markings)
requirements.evidence: No dial, face markings or second axle for a separate minute hand were built. The catalog has no clock face or hand part, so the time cannot be read from this build.

finish.summary: The configurator has no clock-face or clock-hand parts, so this is a partial approximation. The build is two full hex bases with a rod-socket pair and one spool axle carrying a filament spool as a stand-in turning hand. check_build reports meshClash clear and no rule errors. It lacks a wall mount, a dial, a second hand, and any way to read the time.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
